citation.title: Experimental evidence for the key role of the ion heat channel in the physics of the L–H transition
citation.authors: F. Ryter, L. Barrera Orte, B. Kurzan, R.M. McDermott, G. Tardini, E. Viezzer, M. Bernert, R. Fischer and The ASDEX Upgrade Team

topic: Edge ion heat flux and the L–H transition in ASDEX Upgrade. The analysis uses CXRS Ti from short NBI blips and TRANSP power balance.
own_question: Does the edge ion heat flux, rather than the electron heat flux, govern L–H transition access in the low-density branch? Can this explain the density at which the threshold power is minimum?
actual_method_and_evidence: About 25 L–H and 13 H–L transitions were analysed offline with time-dependent TRANSP power balance. Heating was ECRH, NBI, or NBI+ECRH. Edge CXRS ran at 2 ms resolution and core CXRS at 4 ms; NBI blips were needed for Ti in ECRH plasmas. The fitted edge ion heat flux at the transition was about 0.18 times line-averaged density. A scaling for the minimum-threshold density was derived and compared across devices. The authors state that the link to Er and the turbulence mechanism is not quantitatively established.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Edge ion temperature and the ion heat channel are considered physically important to L–H transition access.
claim_checks.qualification: Based on ASDEX Upgrade, low-density branch, deuterium. The Er link is the authors' interpretation. CXRS Ti here is impurity-based, not directly main-ion Ti.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In ECRH-heated plasmas, CXRS ion temperature can be sampled only intermittently, during short NBI blips.
claim_checks.qualification: Applies to the AUG diagnostic setup; the blip spacing limited the time correction of the ion heat flux. Not KSTAR, and not report arrival latency.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Offline power-balance analysis. No nowcasting, no BES/ECEI input, and no real-time processing.
validation_if_relevant: Not applicable; the scalings are empirical fits without held-out validation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not infer KSTAR relevance or results.
Do not infer that nowcasting improves L–H control.
Do not treat CES Ti as main-ion truth.
Do not cite the paper's 2 ms and 4 ms CXRS resolution as our timing.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional single motivation citation for the physical importance of edge Ti. It offers nothing on the estimation method.
